decision.rationale: Je lis d’abord la source de référence la plus rapide mesurée afin de choisir une intégration compatible, sans présumer qu’une autre variante s’y combine utilement.
Je vérifie le code de l’intégration mesurée Gm1 pour déterminer si son raccourci ASCII peut s’adapter au candidat AVX2, plutôt que de combiner des algorithmes complets concurrents.

Partir du meilleur candidat mesuré et correct, c010 (7,78 µs). Adapter uniquement l’idée de 86bba : dans la boucle AVX2, sauter un bloc complet de 32 octets si tous ses octets sont ASCII et qu’aucune continuation n’est attendue (`pending == 0`). Conserver les vérifications existantes pour les autres blocs, les replis SSE2/scalaires et le traitement borné de la queue. Gm1 entier était correct mais plus lent (17,05 µs) : ne pas reprendre son algorithme complet. Mesurer cette intégration et ne la retenir que si elle reste correcte et améliore le temps whole-call.

Base this experiment on 384, the fastest measured correct candidate (7.025 µs), retaining its gated AVX2 checks, scalar boundaries/tail, and fallback. Combine only bf7’s runtime-dispatched AVX-512 path (8.238 µs standalone) to test whether the wider path benefits when paired with the stronger base; keep 384’s AVX2 path as the fallback. The standalone result is slower, so this is a measured compatibility/performance test, not an assumed improvement. Do not include the much slower scalar word-at-a-time or paired-block alternatives.

L’intégration AVX-512 est correcte mais légèrement plus lente que la base 384 (7,263 contre 7,025 µs). Avant de conclure, lire la variante 081, correcte et proche en temps (7,104 µs), pour voir si elle porte une transformation compatible à tester avec la base, plutôt que d’écarter des alternatives non examinées.

Use 384 as the fastest measured correct base (7.025 µs). Its bounded AVX2 path gates special-byte checks but uses unsigned-comparison helpers; 081 is also correct and close in time (7.104 µs), and its source uses direct signed byte comparisons for those bounds. Test that narrow adaptation inside 384’s existing gated branch, preserving its structural checks, scalar boundaries/tail, dispatch, and output contract. Drop the prior AVX-512 combination for this attempt: it was correct but slower at 7.263 µs. These trial means do not establish the new candidate’s performance; controller evaluation is required.

The signed-comparison integration is correct and measured at 6.989 µs, only slightly faster than 384’s 7.025 µs. Before deciding whether further integration is useful, inspect the distinct, correct 8.456 µs variant a882 for a compatible transformation not covered by that experiment.

Keep 62a, the fastest measured correct integration so far (6.989 µs), including its gated special-lead checks. Test one transformation from a882: replace the AVX2 expected-continuation lead-class masks with three exclusive-range masks. a882 is correct but slower standalone (8.456 µs), and its result does not isolate this change; applying it to the stronger base tests whether the simpler masks help in combination. Retain the current scalar boundaries, bounded loads, dispatch, and output contract; require controller evaluation before drawing conclusions.

The latest integration is correct but slower (7.088 µs) than 62a (6.989 µs). Before choosing another transformation, inspect diverse archived trials for a distinct, compatible idea rather than repeating the range-mask change.
